question: Throwing away consumer goods and products instead of repairing and reusing them has a huge impact on the environment as it generates 35 million tonnes of waste every year in the EU. The right to repair is considered an essential step in the EU’s strategy for the transition towards a circular economy by 2050 in the context of the European Green Deal, with the ultimate goal of making the EU climate neutral by 2050.
What is the Commission doing to incentivise EU citizens to repair and reuse consumer goods with a view to reducing waste?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (19.3.2024) On 1 February 2024, co-legislators reached a provisional political agreement1 regarding the Commission’s Proposal for a Directive on common rules promoting the repair of goods2. The Proposal aims at encouraging consumers to use their goods for longer and preventing premature disposal of repairable goods. It establishes a number of measures to promote repair.

Firstly, manufacturers of products (e.g., fridges or smartphones) that are subject to reparability requirements in EU law will have to repair those products upon consumer’s request, within a reasonable time and for a reasonable price. Secondly, consumers will be able to find repairers more easily through a new online European Repair Platform.

Finally, consumers will have a right to an extra year of the legal guarantee if they choose to repair the product instead of replacing it under the legal guarantee. For consumers to benefit from the manufacturer’s obligation to repair, the products must be reparable by design and spare parts must be available.

In this context, the Ecodesign for Sustainable Product Regulation (ESPR) proposal3, on which a political agreement4 was reached in December 2023, will establish a framework for setting requirements on reparability or reusability for a wide range of products on the EU market.

These will cover, for example, the availability of spare parts, and may also cover information requirements, enabling consumers to make informed choices, in particular through a digital product passport.
1 For more information: https://ec.europa.eu/commission/presscorner/detail/en/ip_24_608 2 For more information: https://commission.europa.eu/law/law-topic/consumer-protection-law/consumer-
